land.text: Mercia's first Cliopatria shape: 104 of its 105 cells lie in the anglo-saxon-england dossier's successor land for Mercia

predecessors.note: The anglo-saxon-england dossier (441-533) names this state as its successor with the land of Mercia's 534 shape. This dossier starts at 527 (infobox 'Established: 527'), six years before anglo-saxon-england dissolves in 533, and anglo-saxon-england has a 527 split for Essex but none for Mercia: the land is claimed by both states for 527-533 until that dossier's owner adds the split.

union.text: the 911 shape: the western half without Oxford

land.text: Mercia as it stood in 918 (the western half without Oxford, plus Derby and Leicester), taken by Edward the Elder

successors.note: Edward 'took Mercia under his control' in early December 918; the later shires were made from it ('divided it into shires'). The eastern half had gone to the Danelaw in 877 (slug danelaw).

capitals.name: Tamworth
capitals.note: Creoda, 'coming to power around 584, ... built a fortress at Tamworth which became the seat of Mercia's kings'; the page also says the royal court 'moved around the kingdom without a fixed capital city'. Æthelflæd died at Tamworth on 12 June 918. No seat is named for 527-583.

correction.text: unchanged; the shape should run from 527 (infobox 'Established: 527') to 576

keyframe_review.note: The infobox gives no area, so the Cliopatria figure cannot be checked against it. 23,472 km2 for the East Midlands core. Only the years change: the infobox has 'Established: 527', Cliopatria starts in 534.

23,926 km2: five cells added in the centre (1.8-1.5 W, 52.2-52.7 N) and two dropped in the south-west (2.0-1.8 W, 51.9 N; the Hwicce row begins in 577). The Mercia page is silent on 577; unverified: page budget.
27,284 km2: a 3.5 thousand km2 addition on the north-west edge that the Mercia page does not explain (ledger 617 at confidence 1). Unverified: page budget.
37,633 km2: contains the whole Hwicce shape (Cirencester, 628, page-dated, ledger 628) plus about 7 thousand km2 more that no opened page explains (ledger 628, confidence 1).
Same land as 628 (one cell more). Penda's reign ends with the Winwaed in 655; this shape stands to 655.

correction.text: Mercia from the 658 revolt, as in 647-655: 'A Mercian revolt in 658 threw off Northumbrian domination'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years Cliopatria leaves blank: Mercia has no shape for 656-660 and Northumbria's 85,405 km2 shape covers it. Oswiu took 'direct control of the whole of Mercia' in 656 and 'A Mercian revolt in 658 threw off Northumbrian domination'. 656-657 stay Northumbrian (ledger 656), Mercia is drawn again from 658.

38,119 km2: the 647 land plus two cells, the Isle of Wight, which Wulfhere raided in 661. The Wihtwara page has him conquer it in 661 and give the overlordship to Æthelwealh of Sussex, so the island is removed from Mercia's own land (ledger 661, gain and loss); Cliopatria keeps it until 665. He was 'the effective overlord of Britain south of the Humber from the early 660s'.

correction.text: Mercia without the Isle of Wight, which Wulfhere conquered and handed to Æthelwealh of Sussex in 661
Mercia without Essex; Essex is a client under Wulfhere from 664

keyframe_review.note: 41,436 km2: the 661 shape (corrected: Cliopatria drops the island only here, in 666; the ledger moves its loss to 661), plus Essex (16 cells, Essex's own shape, which ends in 665). The page says the East Saxon kings ruled 'under Wulfhere' from 664: a client with kings of its own. Corrected to the Mercian land proper; Essex is drawn as a vassal through the ledger (664 to 825).

correction.text: Mercia with Lindsey, without Essex

keyframe_review.note: 45,347 km2: adds Lindsey (17 cells) after the Battle of the Trent, 679 (page-dated; Cliopatria lags three years). Essex is removed as in 666.

correction.text: Mercia without Essex

keyframe_review.note: 45,435 km2: two cells added near London (506 km2); no opened page dates them. Essex removed as in 666.

correction.text: Mercia with the Wroxeter region, without Essex

keyframe_review.note: 48,306 km2: adds the Welsh border strip around Wroxeter ('At some point before the accession of Æthelbald in 716 the Mercians conquered the region around Wroxeter'; ledger 705, three events at confidence 1: 11 cells, 5 from Powys at Wroxeter, 5 from Gwynedd on the Dee plain, 1 from Gwent at Archenfield). Essex removed as in 666.

correction.text: Mercia without Wessex (hegemony, not annexation) and Essex

keyframe_review.note: 74,610 km2: this is Mercia's 755 land plus Wessex's whole 740 shape (100 cells). Æthelbald's hegemony 'over the rest of the Anglo-Saxons south of the Humber' (after 726) is overlordship; Wessex kept its kings and beat him in 752. Corrected to Mercia without Wessex or Essex; Wessex is a vassal through the ledger (726 to 752).

correction.text: Mercia without Essex

keyframe_review.note: 48,306 km2, the same land as 705-740. Wessex is its own shape again after Cuthred's victory (752). Essex removed as in 666; Cynewulf of Wessex 'recovered much of the border territory' from 757 (ledger 757, Cliopatria shows it in 763).

correction.text: Mercia without the clients Kent and Essex

keyframe_review.note: 50,797 km2: adds Kent (17 cells) and loses 9 cells of Thames border land to Wessex. Offa's influence in Kent is first attested in 764 (charter at Rochester with Heahberht as king of Kent): a client, not annexation. Corrected to remove Kent and Essex.

correction.text: Mercia with Sussex, without Kent and Essex

keyframe_review.note: 56,170 km2: adds Sussex (23 cells) after Offa 'defeated the people of Hastings' in 771 (ledger 771, taken as annexation as the Sussex dossier does). Kent and Essex removed as clients.

correction.text: Mercia with Sussex and the Bensington strip, without Kent and Essex

keyframe_review.note: 57,851 km2: gets back 9 cells of Oxfordshire border land (Bensington, 779). Kent and Essex removed as clients.

correction.text: Mercia with Sussex, without the clients Wessex, Kent and Essex

keyframe_review.note: 84,530 km2: the 783 land plus Wessex's whole 787 shape (102 cells). Offa 'may have intervened to place Beorhtric on the West Saxon throne' in 786: overlordship at most. Wessex, Kent and Essex removed.

minus.text: Wessex (its 787 shape), Kent, Essex, East Anglia

correction.text: Mercia with Sussex, without the clients Wessex, Kent, Essex and East Anglia

keyframe_review.note: 96,899 km2, the peak: Mercia plus Wessex, Kent, Essex and East Anglia (55 cells added since 788). Offa had Æthelberht of East Anglia beheaded in 794; Beorhtric of Wessex died in 802. Clients removed: Wessex's 787 shape (not its 806 shape, so that the three Thames cells west of London that Wessex loses in 806 are not Mercian before the 806 gain), Kent, Essex and East Anglia; East Anglia is a vassal through the ledger (794 to 796 and c. 799 to 825) and Kent likewise (798 to 825).

correction.text: Mercia with Sussex, without Kent, Essex and East Anglia

keyframe_review.note: 70,879 km2: Wessex has its own shape again (806), Kent and East Anglia are still inside this one. Clients removed as in 800. The three Thames cells west of London are Mercian from here (ledger 806, gain from Wessex).

correction.text: unchanged, but only for 825-828: 'In 829, Ecgberht invaded Mercia and drove Wiglaf, the king of Mercia, into exile'

keyframe_review.note: 44,460 km2 after Ellandun (825): Kent, Sussex, Essex, Surrey and East Anglia submit to Wessex. Cliopatria's shape runs to 829; Ecgberht conquered Mercia in 829, so it should end in 828 (ledger 829).

correction.text: Mercia as in 825-829, independent under Wiglaf from 830

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Mercia for 830-839 and draws a 96,899 km2 Wessex shape (Wessex, Mercia, East Anglia, Kent, Sussex). 'In 830, Mercia regained its independence under Wiglaf.' Essex is not in the Mercian shape until 840 (ledger 840).
48,371 km2: the 825 land plus the Essex-London area (ledger 840, confidence 1; the Wessex dossier has the same shift on Cliopatria's year). Beorhtwulf succeeded Wiglaf about 840.
48,418 km2: two cells added on the Welsh border (3.3-3.1 W, 52.7-53.1 N), probably the North Wales gains of 852 ('with Ethelwulf of Wessex subjugated North Wales'; ledger 852 as a vassal).
44,689 km2: loses 4.3 thousand km2 of Lindsey and north Midlands in 866 (ledger 866, confidence 1). Nottingham is still inside (occupied 868).
37,627 km2 after Nottingham (868, 'Danish invaders occupied Nottingham'). Burgred is driven out in 874.

correction.text: Mercia under Ceolwulf II in 875-876: the 870 shape without London and Essex; the western half only from 877

keyframe_review.note: 25,729 km2 for 875-877. The pages date the Danish seizure of the east to 877 ('In 877 the Danes seized the eastern part of Mercia') and Ceolwulf II was given the whole kingdom 'to hold' in 874; London goes to Alfred about 875. For 875-876 the 870 shape without London and Essex; from 877 the western half (the 880 shape).

correction.text: the western half of Mercia, as in 880-883

keyframe_review.note: 30,992 km2 (878-879) is neither the Mercia of 870 nor the western half of 880: the Danes took the east in 877, so 878-879 is the 880 shape. 'Ceolwulf, the last king of Mercia, left with the western half, reigned until 879.' A client of Wessex from 879.

21,745 km2, the western half (it includes Oxford, not London): Ceolwulf II to 879, then 'Æthelred, Lord of the Mercians' from about 883 under Wessex. Drawn as a vassal of Wessex (infobox 'Client state of Wessex (879-918)'); shape unchanged.

correction.text: the western half of Mercia under Æthelred, Lord of the Mercians

keyframe_review.note: 43.7 km2: a residue of one cell. Cliopatria's Wessex shape from 884 (57,728 km2) is Wessex plus essentially the 880 western half of Mercia, which was a Mercian client under Æthelred, not Wessex. Use the 880 shape, with London added from 886 (new keyframe 886).

correction.text: Mercia with London: 'In 886 Alfred occupied the Mercian town of London, which had been in Viking hands'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the western half plus London, which Alfred took from the Danes in 886 and gave to Æthelred.

correction.text: 899-910 as in the 886 keyframe; 911-918 see the 911 and 917 keyframes

keyframe_review.note: 43.7 km2 residue (899-921). Mercia was Æthelred's, then Æthelflæd's until December 918 (new keyframes 886, 911, 917). Use the 886 shape to 910.

correction.text: the western half without Oxford (London is not in it): 'When Æthelred died, Edward took control of the Mercian towns of London and Oxford'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Edward took London and Oxford when Æthelred died in 911; Æthelflæd rules the rest as Lady of the Mercians.

correction.text: the 911 shape with the boroughs of Derby (917) and Leicester (918)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Æthelflæd takes Derby (917) and Leicester (918) from the Danes before she dies on 12 June 918; Edward takes Mercia in December 918.

correction.text: no Mercia from 919: its land is in the Wessex shape under Edward the Elder

keyframe_review.note: 43.7 km2 residue (922-925). 'in early December 918 Edward deposed her and took Mercia under his control'; Mercia has no shape after 918. Cliopatria's Wessex shape from 922 (96,296 km2) holds the land.

region.text: Mercia's core as Cliopatria draws it from 534 (East Midlands); the page names no land

ledger.note: 527: the kingdom of Mercia is established under Icel. Infobox 'Established: 527'; ruler list '527-c. 535: Icel (first)'. The page names no boundary and gives no area; the region is Cliopatria's first shape (from 534) read as the kingdom's core.

region.text: the north-west addition of Cliopatria's 617 shape; page silent

ledger.note: 617: Cliopatria's shape grows about 3.5 thousand km2 to the north-west (bounding box 2.8-2.0 W, 52.9-53.4 N). The Mercia page does not date or explain this growth (it gives Cearl's accession in 606 and his daughter's marriage to Edwin of Deira in 615); recorded at confidence 1, with the Cliopatria neighbour on that edge as counterpart.

region.text: the Hwicce, 'the formerly West Saxon territories of Hwicce'

ledger.note: 628: Penda takes the Hwicce country after Cirencester: 'following the Battle of Cirencester of 628, when Penda incorporated the formerly West Saxon territories of Hwicce'. The Wulfhere page adds that the Hwicce were later 'already subordinate to Wulfhere', so their kings went on as sub-rulers.

region.text: the part of the 628 shape that is neither the 617 shape nor the Hwicce; page silent

ledger.note: 628: Cliopatria's shape adds a further 7 thousand km2 across the Midlands (2.9-0.8 W, 51.7-53.5 N) beyond the Hwicce. The Mercia page dates only the Hwicce acquisition in Penda's reign ('about 626 or 633 until 655'); this part is Cliopatria's and rests on no opened page.

656: Oswiu of Northumbria takes Mercia after Penda's fall at the Winwaed (15 November 655, Wulfhere page). 'in the spring of 656 he [Peada] was murdered and Oswiu assumed direct control of the whole of Mercia.' Cliopatria draws the whole of Mercia inside Northumbria's 85,405 km2 shape for 656-660.

658: Mercia throws off Northumbrian rule under Wulfhere. 'A Mercian revolt in 658 threw off Northumbrian domination'; the Wulfhere page: 'Wulfhere came to the throne when Mercian nobles organized a revolt against Northumbrian rule in 658'. Cliopatria keeps Mercia inside Northumbria's shape until 660 and has no Mercia shape for 656-660.

region.text: the Isle of Wight, raided in 661

ledger.note: 661: Wulfhere takes the Isle of Wight. 'In addition to the attack on Ashdown, Wulfhere raided the Isle of Wight in 661.' The page says he 'subsequently gave both the island and the territory of the Meonware' to Æthelwealh of the South Saxons, so Mercian rule was brief; Cliopatria's 661 shape adds exactly the two cells of the island. Given away in the same year: see the 661 loss.

region.text: the Meonware, the Meon valley and the Hampshire coast beyond the later county of Sussex (the western extension of Cliopatria's Sussex shape, as the Sussex dossier draws it)

ledger.note: 661: Wulfhere takes the Meon valley with the Isle of Wight. 'He conquered the Isle of Wight and the Meon valley and gave them to King Æthelwealh of the South Saxons'; the page dates the raid on the island to 661 and the gift to no year, and does not say whom the Meonware territory was taken from, so the counterpart is 'nobody' (no Meonware king is named; the Sussex page calls Wight and the Meonwara 'provinces'). Cliopatria's Mercia shape never holds the valley (its Sussex shape has it from 490), so no keyframe changes; Mercian rule was brief, see the 661 loss.

region.text: the island, given to Æthelwealh, with the Meon valley

ledger.note: 661: Wulfhere gives the Isle of Wight and the Meon valley to Æthelwealh of Sussex. The Wihtwara page: 'in 661 Wulfhere of Mercia conquered the Isle of Wight' and 'gave the overlordship to his godson, King Æthelwealh of Sussex', to convert the islanders. The Wulfhere page says only that he 'subsequently gave both the island and the territory of the Meonware, which lay along the river Meon' to Æthelwealh, with no year, and the Kingdom of Sussex page gives none either. Moved here from 666 (Cliopatria's year, the first shape without the island) because the wihtgar and kingdom-of-sussex dossiers both date the gift to 661. The island passes to Sussex as overlord (wihtgar is Sussex's vassal from 661); the Meon valley is Sussex land.

region.text: the East Saxon kingdom under Sigehere and Sæbbi

ledger.note: 664: the East Saxon kings rule under Wulfhere. Bede 'describes the 664 accession of Sigehere and Sæbbi as rulers ... under Wulfhere, king of the Mercians'; Wulfhere 'seems to have been the effective overlord of Britain south of the Humber from the early 660s' and between 665 and 668 sold the see of London to Wine. The Mercian Supremacy page calls Mercia's hold on Essex, Sussex and Kent 'tenuous until 716, when Æthelbald ... restored Mercia's hegemony for over forty years'. Cliopatria's Essex row ends 665 and Mercia's shape takes its land from 666.

674: Wulfhere loses Lindsey to Northumbria and the fight for it begins. 'Ecgfrith defeated Wulfhere, forcing him to surrender Lindsey, and to pay tribute' (the page dates Wulfhere's attack on Ecgfrith to 674). The Mercian Supremacy page dates the loss of Lindsey to 661 instead; Cliopatria draws Lindsey inside Northumbria from 626 to 681.

region.text: Lindsey, the ground of the Trent campaign

ledger.note: 679: Æthelred beats Ecgfrith at the Trent. 'The Mercians were victorious, ending Northumbrian domination of the area'; the infobox dates the battle 'c. 679'.

679: Æthelred takes Lindsey for Mercia: he 'defeated Northumbria in the Battle of the Trent in 679', settling 'the long-disputed control of the former kingdom of Lindsey'. The Trent page: 'Lindsey would from then on become a client state of Mercia'; the Lindsey page says it was absorbed into Mercia in the 8th century, without a year. Cliopatria adds Lindsey to Mercia's shape in 682.

region.text: east Kent under Oswine, 'probably supported by Æthelred of Mercia'; the whole Kentish shape

ledger.note: 688: Oswine takes the Kentish throne with Mercian backing. 'When Cædwalla departed for Rome in 688, Oswine, who was probably supported by Æthelred of Mercia, took the throne for a time.' The Kingdom of Kent page calls him a 'client king' and has him reigning about two years; the Wihtred page: 'It seems that Oswine was king of east Kent', Swæfheard son of Sebbi of Essex king of west Kent. Mercia is the overlord and the counterpart is the vassal (the Kent dossier records the same relation from its side, 688 to 691).

c. 691: Wihtred succeeds and Oswine's Mercian-backed kingship ends. 'The overlap in date ranges gives April to July 691 as the likely date of his accession.' The page does not say that Mercian overlordship stopped; the end is a bridge, as in the Kent dossier (confidence 1).

region.text: the Welsh border strip around Wroxeter: the part of Mercia's 705 addition that lay inside Powys's shape (5 cells, 1,264 km2)

ledger.note: 705: the Welsh border strip around Wroxeter passes to Mercia in Cliopatria's shape. The page says only: 'At some point before the accession of Æthelbald in 716 the Mercians conquered the region around Wroxeter'; 705 is Cliopatria's year. Split from one event into three on 2026-10-25: Mercia's 705 addition is 11 cells, of which 5 lie inside Powys's shape (this event), 5 inside Gwynedd's 704 shape and 1 inside Gwent's 704 shape (the next two events), as the three neighbour dossiers record their losses to Mercia in 705.

region.text: the Dee plain on the Cheshire-Flintshire border: the part of Mercia's 705 addition that lay inside Gwynedd's 704 shape (5 cells, 1,264 km2)

ledger.note: 705: the Dee plain passes to Mercia in Cliopatria's shape. The Mercia page (re-read 2026-10-25) dates no Gwynedd loss to Mercia: it says only that Ceolwulf attacked and destroyed the fortress of Deganwy in Gwynedd, a raid and not a conquest; 705 is Cliopatria's year, and the Gwynedd dossier records the same year at confidence 1. Five of the seven cells the Gwynedd dossier lists as lost in 705 are in Mercia's 705 shape; the other two (lon -3.65 to -2.94, lat 52.95 to 53.38) are not in any Mercian shape and have no Mercian event.

region.text: the Archenfield cell on the Wye (lon -2.71, lat 51.83): the part of Mercia's 705 addition that lay inside Gwent's 704 shape (1 cell, 253 km2)

ledger.note: 705: the Archenfield cell passes to Mercia in Cliopatria's shape. The Mercia page (re-read 2026-10-25) does not mention Gwent or Archenfield; 705 is Cliopatria's year, and the Gwent dossier records the same year at confidence 1.

726: Æthelbald makes Mercia the leading power south of the Humber, Wessex included. 'when Wihtred died in 725, and Ine abdicated in 726 to become a monk in Rome', Æthelbald 'was free to establish Mercia's hegemony over the rest of the Anglo-Saxons south of the Humber.' Overlordship, not annexation; Cliopatria draws Wessex inside Mercia's shape only from 741 to 754 (Wessex has its own shape to 740).
752: Wessex throws off Mercian hegemony. 'Æthelbald suffered a setback in 752, when the West Saxons under Cuthred defeated him'. Cliopatria's Wessex shape returns in 755.

region.text: the border land between the Chilterns and the upper Thames lost in Cliopatria's 763 shape

ledger.note: 757: the West Saxons recover the border strip on the Thames. Cynewulf 'came to the throne of Wessex in 757 and recovered much of the border territory'; the page does not date the recovery inside his reign, and 757 is his accession. Cliopatria's Mercia drops 2.3 thousand km2 (1.3-0.2 W, 51.6-51.8 N) in 763 and Cliopatria's Wessex gains about 1.9 thousand km2 in the same year.

region.text: the Kentish kingdom, last Cliopatria shape

ledger.note: 764: Offa's influence in Kent is first attested. 'In 764, Offa granted land at Rochester in his own name, with Heahberht on the witness list as king of Kent.' Kentish kings continued, so Kent is a Mercian client, not a Mercian province; the page records the fight at Otford in 776 (outcome not recorded) and charters of 785-89 that 'make his authority clear', and says 'Mercian control lasted until 796'. The breaks in this span (776 to 785, 796 to 798) are the next events; the Mercia page puts the final loss of Kent at 825.

771: Offa conquers Sussex. 'Symeon of Durham ... records that in 771 Offa defeated the people of Hastings'; Cliopatria gives Mercia the whole of Sussex's shape from 772 and ends the Sussex row in 771. The page adds: 'After 772, there is no further evidence of Mercian involvement in Sussex until c. 790.'

776: Kent slips out of Mercian authority at Otford. The Kingdom of Kent page: 'A battle was fought at Otford in 776, and although the outcome is unknown,' 'Egbert II and later Ealhmund seem to have ruled independently of Offa for nearly a decade thereafter.' The Offa page (read 2026-10-25) records the fight ('the Mercians and the inhabitants of Kent fought at Otford') without an outcome, calls the traditional reading a Mercian victory, and says 'there is no evidence for Offa's authority over Kent until 785'. Confidence 2: the year is the battle's; that the vassalage ended there is the Kent page's reading of what followed.

region.text: the Oxfordshire border strip Cliopatria returns to Mercia in 783

ledger.note: 779: Offa wins the Thames-valley border strip back at Bensington: 'Offa won an important victory over Cynewulf at the Battle of Bensington (in Oxfordshire) in 779.' The page does not say what land changed hands; Cliopatria returns the strip to Mercia in 783 (9 cells, 2.3 thousand km2).

785: Offa re-establishes his authority over Kent. 'There is no evidence for Offa's authority over Kent until 785' and 'a sequence of charters by Offa from the years 785-89 makes his authority clear', treating Kent 'as an ordinary province of the Mercian kingdom'; the Kingdom of Kent page: 'Offa firmly re-established his authority over Kent in 785.' Kept as a client, as the Kent dossier and the 764 event do; the page's 'ordinary province' could also be read as direct rule 785 to 796.

786: Offa and Wessex. 'In 786, after the murder of Cynewulf, Offa may have intervened to place Beorhtric on the West Saxon throne'; in 789 Beorhtric married Eadburh, Offa's daughter. Hedged on the page ('may'); Cliopatria folds Wessex into Mercia's shape from 788 to 805.

794: Offa has the East Anglian king executed and rules East Anglia. 'In 794, according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, King Offa ordered King Æthelberht's head to be struck off.' The revival of 796 to c. 799 that this page does not mention is recorded in the next events (Kingdom of East Anglia page); Cliopatria draws East Anglia inside Mercia from 800.

796: Offa dies and Kent rebels. 'Mercian control lasted until 796, the year of Offa's death,' when 'Eadberht Præn was temporarily successful in regaining Kentish independence.' The Mercia page's 825 (the next vassal_end) is the final loss; this event closes the first span.

796: East Anglia revives after Offa's death. Infobox: 'Independent (6th century-794; 796-c. 799; 825-869)' and 'Client state of Mercia (794-796; c. 799-825)'; 'A brief revival of East Anglian independence under Eadwald, after Offa's death in 796, was suppressed by the new Mercian king, Coenwulf.' The Offa page (read 2026-10-25) says nothing of East Anglia after 796. Confidence 2: the page dates the revival to Offa's death; Eadwald is not dated more closely.

798: Coenwulf reconquers Kent. 'Offa's eventual successor, Coenwulf, reconquered Kent in 798, however, and installed his brother Cuthred as king.' The Coenwulf page: the Pope's authorisation 'was delayed until 798', then 'Coenwulf invaded and retook the kingdom'; 'By 801 at the latest Coenwulf had placed his brother, Cuthred, on the throne of Kent', and after Cuthred's death in 807 Coenwulf 'took control of Kent in name as well as fact' (direct rule 807 to 825 is not split off here; Kent stays a client to 825, as in the Kent dossier).

c. 799: Coenwulf suppresses Eadwald and East Anglia is a Mercian client again. Infobox 'Client state of Mercia (794-796; c. 799-825)'; the page dates the suppression no closer. The Coenwulf page says only that 'In East Anglia, King Eadwald minted coins at about this time, implying that he was no longer subject to Mercia'.

802: Wessex leaves Mercian overlordship. The page is silent on the end of the arrangement: 'Beorhtric died in 802, and Ecgberht came to the throne of Wessex.' Cliopatria's Wessex shape resumes in 806.

region.text: three cells of the Thames west of London (lon -0.65 to -0.05, lat 51.46 to 51.57), in Wessex's shape to 805 and in Mercia's from 806

ledger.note: 806: three cells of the Thames west of London pass from Wessex to Mercia in Cliopatria's shapes. The Mercian Supremacy page (re-read 2026-10-25) names no Mercian-West Saxon conflict or border change between 796 and 825 (page silent); the Wessex dossier records the loss in the same year at confidence 1. Until 806 the cells are Wessex land: the 800 keyframe now subtracts Wessex's 787 shape, not its 806 shape.

825: Ellandun ends the Mercian Supremacy. 'In 825, Ecgberht defeated Beornwulf of Mercia, ended Mercian Supremacy at the Battle of Ellandun' and 'the men of Kent, Essex, Surrey and Sussex then all submitted'. The Mercia page: 'At this point, Mercia lost control of Kent, Sussex, Surrey, and possibly also Essex.' Kent leaves Mercian overlordship for Wessex.

825: Essex leaves Mercian overlordship. 'the men of Kent, Essex, Surrey and Sussex then all submitted to Æthelwulf'; the page adds that Ecgberht expelled King Sigered of Essex on an unknown date and that Wessex may not have held Essex. The Mercia page has 'possibly also Essex'.

825: East Anglia leaves Mercian overlordship. 'the East Anglians asked for Ecgberht's protection against the Mercians in the same year, 825'; 'The outcome in East Anglia was a disaster for the Mercians'. Beornwulf (826) and Ludeca (827) died trying to recover it.

825: Sussex goes to Wessex. 'the men of Kent, Essex, Surrey and Sussex then all submitted to Æthelwulf'; the Mercia page: 'At this point, Mercia lost control of Kent, Sussex, Surrey, and possibly also Essex.' Cliopatria's 825 shape drops 27.6 thousand km2 (Kent, Sussex, Essex, East Anglia).

829: Ecgberht of Wessex conquers Mercia. 'In 829, Ecgberht invaded Mercia and drove Wiglaf, the king of Mercia, into exile'; the Chronicle entry: 'conquered the kingdom of Mercia, and all that was south of the Humber'. He took the London mint and issued coins as King of Mercia.

830: Wiglaf restores Mercia. 'In 830, Mercia regained its independence under Wiglaf'; the Chronicle says Wiglaf 'obtained the kingdom of Mercia again'. Cliopatria has no Mercia shape for 830-839 and draws a 96,899 km2 Wessex shape over it.

region.text: the Essex and London area added by Cliopatria's 840 shape

ledger.note: 840: Cliopatria adds the Essex-London area (4.3 thousand km2, 0.6 W-0.7 E, 51.5-51.9 N) to Mercia. The Egbert page says only that he 'expelled King Sigered' of Essex on an unknown date and that Wessex may not have held Essex; the Mercia page dates Beorhtwulf's accession c. 840 and nothing about land. Recorded at confidence 1 on Cliopatria's year.

852: Mercia and Wessex subject North Wales. 'In 852, Burgred came to the throne, and with Ethelwulf of Wessex subjugated North Wales.' The page names no boundary; Cliopatria's Mercia shape gains two cells on the Welsh border in 860.

region.text: the north-east Midlands and Lindsey dropped by Cliopatria's 866 shape

ledger.note: 866: Cliopatria takes about 4.3 thousand km2 of north Midlands and Lindsey (0.9 W-0.1 E, 52.6-53.5 N) from Mercia in 866, the year its Viking settlements shape first touches Mercia. No opened page dates the Danish hold on this land (the Mercia page has Nottingham in 868 and Repton in 874).

region.text: Nottingham and the East Midlands lost in Cliopatria's 870 shape

ledger.note: 868: the Danes occupy Nottingham. 'In 868 Danish invaders occupied Nottingham.' The Danelaw page has Burgred ceding Nottingham in 867 'in exchange for leaving the rest of Mercia undisturbed' and the Danes capturing it in 868. Cliopatria's shape loses 8.1 thousand km2 around it in 870.

874: the Danes drive Burgred out and set up Ceolwulf II. 'The Danes drove Burgred from his kingdom in 874 and Ceolwulf II took his place'; the Chronicle: 'they gave Ceolwulf, an unwise king's thane, the Mercian kingdom to hold'. Burgred had reigned from 852.

region.text: London and the East Saxon country

ledger.note: 875: London passes to Alfred: 'in about 875, Alfred was the sole recognised ruler in London'. Cliopatria's 875 shape drops the London and Essex cells and a further 10 thousand km2 elsewhere that no opened page explains; the pages date the loss of the east to 877.

region.text: the eastern part of Mercia seized by the Danes

ledger.note: 877: the Danes take the eastern half of Mercia. 'In 877 the Danes seized the eastern part of Mercia, which became part of the Danelaw.' 'Ceolwulf, the last king of Mercia, left with the western half'. Cliopatria shows the western half as the 880 shape.

879: the last king ends and Mercia becomes a client of Wessex. 'Ceolwulf, the last king of Mercia, left with the western half, reigned until 879'; infobox 'Independent kingdom (527-879)', 'Client state of Wessex (879-918)'. The Ceolwulf page notes Kirby's view that he 'probably reigned into the early 880s'.

region.text: English Mercia, the western half of the kingdom, which is the client

ledger.note: 879: Mercia becomes a client state of Wessex. Mercia infobox: 'Independent kingdom (527-879) Client state of Wessex (879-918)'; body: 'From about 883 until his death in 911 Æthelred, Lord of the Mercians, ruled Mercia under the overlordship of Wessex'; the Æthelflæd page: 'In 883, he made a grant with the consent of King Alfred, thus acknowledging Alfred's lordship.' Direction: here Mercia is the client and the counterpart names its overlord, the reverse of the 726-752 and 786-802 pairs (where Wessex is the vassal); the Wessex dossier records the same relation with Mercia as the counterpart and the region (880 to 918). Confidence 2: the infobox says 879, the body 883, the Wessex dossier 880.

881: North Wales shakes off Mercia. 'In 881 Rhodri's sons defeated the Mercians at the Battle of the Conwy'; Rhodri Mawr had been killed fighting the English in 878. The page does not call this the end of an overlordship; the year is the battle's.

883: Æthelred rules Mercia as Lord of the Mercians under Wessex. 'From about 883 until his death in 911 Æthelred, Lord of the Mercians, ruled Mercia under the overlordship of Wessex'; the Aethelflaed page: 'In 883, he made a grant with the consent of King Alfred, thus acknowledging Alfred's lordship.'

886: Alfred takes London from the Danes and gives it to Æthelred. 'In 886 Alfred occupied the Mercian town of London, which had been in Viking hands.' The Mercia page: Alfred had placed London and Oxford under Æthelred's control.
911: Æthelred dies and his widow Æthelflæd rules Mercia as Lady of the Mercians: 'Æthelred died in 911 and Æthelflæd then ruled Mercia as Lady of the Mercians.'

region.text: the towns of London and Oxford

ledger.note: 911: Edward the Elder takes London and Oxford: 'When Æthelred died, Edward took control of the Mercian towns of London and Oxford.' The Mercia page: Edward 'took control of London and Oxford, which Alfred had placed under Æthelred's control'.

917: Æthelflæd takes Derby from the Danes: 'Æthelflæd, Lady of the Mercians, took the borough of Derby.' The Aethelflaed page: 'In 917 invasions by three Viking armies failed as Æthelflæd sent an army which captured' it.

918: Leicester submits to Æthelflæd. 'In 918 Leicester surrendered without a fight'; the Danelaw page: 'The borough of Leicester submitted peaceably to Æthelflæd's rule.' York's leaders offered her their loyalty but she died first.

region.text: English Mercia, the western half of the kingdom, which is the client

ledger.note: December 918: Edward the Elder ends Mercia's client status by taking it into his own hands. Æthelflæd died at Tamworth on 12 June 918; 'in early December 918 Edward deposed her [her daughter Ælfwynn] and took Mercia under his control.' The Mercia infobox closes the client state in 918. Direction as in the 879 event: Mercia is the client; the Wessex dossier has the same end (918, Mercia as counterpart).

union.text: the 911 shape: the western half without Oxford

region.text: Mercia as it stood in 918: the western half without Oxford (taken by Edward in 911), plus Derby and Leicester

ledger.note: 918: Edward the Elder ends Mercia. Æthelflæd died at Tamworth on 12 June 918; 'in early December 918 Edward deposed her [her daughter Ælfwynn] and took Mercia under his control.' The Mercia infobox gives 'Annexed by Wessex: 918'; Cliopatria keeps a 44 km2 Mercia residue to 925.

wars.name: Penda's wars with Northumbria

zones.text: the Mercian heartland, ruled by Oswiu 656-658

wars.outcome: Penda and Cadwallon of Gwynedd defeated and killed Edwin in 633; Maserfield followed in 642; Penda lost battle and life at the Winwaed in 655, Oswiu took direct control of Mercia in 656 and a revolt freed it in 658.
wars.note: The page does not name Hatfield Chase. The Winwaed was fought on 15 November 655 (Wulfhere page).

wars.name: Wulfhere's campaigns in the south

zones.text: the Isle of Wight and Ashdown

wars.outcome: Wulfhere harried Ashdown and raided the Isle of Wight in 661, then gave the island and the Meon valley to Æthelwealh of the South Saxons.
wars.note: The page calls Ashdown 'West Saxon territory'.

wars.name: Battle of the Trent
wars.outcome: Ecgfrith of Northumbria forced Wulfhere to surrender Lindsey (674); Æthelred of Mercia won the Trent in 679 and Lindsey became a client of Mercia. The 18-year-old Ælfwine of Deira was killed; Theodore, Archbishop of Canterbury, intervened to prevent further conflict.
wars.note: The Mercian Supremacy page dates the loss of Lindsey to 661.

wars.name: Offa's wars with Wessex
wars.outcome: Cynewulf recovered border land from 757; Offa won at Bensington in 779 and may have placed Beorhtric on the throne in 786.

wars.name: Offa's campaigns in Kent and Sussex
wars.outcome: Mercian influence in Kent from 764, the fight at Otford in 776 (outcome unrecorded), Hastings defeated in 771, Offa's authority in Kent clear in charters of 785-89.

wars.name: Offa's Welsh campaigns
wars.outcome: Fights at Hereford (760) and campaigns in 778, 784 and 796; Offa's Dyke marks the frontier. No change of border is dated.
wars.note: The Mercia page: 'a dyke was created as the boundary between Mercia and the Welsh kingdoms'; the Offa page: most of it 'probably built in his reign', not archaeologically dated.

wars.name: Battle of Ellandun

zones.text: Kent, Sussex, Essex and East Anglia, lost in 825

wars.outcome: Ecgberht beat Beornwulf in 825; Kent, Essex, Surrey and Sussex submitted and East Anglia sought his protection. Beornwulf (826) and Ludeca (827) died in East Anglia. Ecgberht conquered Mercia in 829 and Wiglaf was back in 830.

wars.name: Mercian and West Saxon conquest of North Wales
wars.outcome: Burgred and Æthelwulf 'subjugated North Wales' in 852; Rhodri Mawr died fighting the English in 878 and his sons beat the Mercians at the Conwy in 881.

wars.name: Danish invasions of Mercia

zones.text: Nottingham, the East Midlands and the east of Mercia

wars.outcome: Nottingham occupied in 868, Burgred driven out in 874, Ceolwulf II installed, the eastern part seized in 877 and joined to the Danelaw; Ceolwulf kept the western half.
wars.note: The Danelaw page has Burgred ceding Nottingham in 867.

wars.name: Æthelflæd's wars with the Danes
wars.outcome: The Danish army was destroyed at Tettenhall (910); Derby fell in 917 and Leicester submitted in 918. Æthelflæd died on 12 June 918.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page opened; the frontier with the Welsh kingdoms and the Hwicce, Lindsey and Essex edges are approximate.

Offa's Dyke, 'created as the boundary between Mercia and the Welsh kingdoms' and 'probably built in his reign', is the one built frontier, but it is not dated and no source gives its line; the Danelaw frontier fixed 'Between 886 and 890' has no boundary list on the page opened.

notes: Cliopatria shows Mercia's 29 shapes with three structural faults: (1) hegemony drawn as annexation (741-754 and 788-805 include Wessex's whole shape, 800-824 East Anglia, Kent and Sussex; 830-839 is a Wessex shape that swallows Mercia); (2) no shapes for 656-660 and 830-839; (3) from 884 a 43.7 km2 residue to 925, while the western half of Mercia (the 880 shape) is folded into Wessex's shape from 884 although it was Æthelred's and Æthelflæd's client state to December 918. Corrections are in keyframe_review; Wessex, Kent, Essex, East Anglia and Gwynedd are vassals through the ledger (Kent in the spans 688-691, 764-776, 785-796 and 798-825; East Anglia 794-796 and c. 799-825), and Mercia is itself a client of Wessex 879-918. Start 527 is the infobox year (Cliopatria starts 534). End December 918 is the Aethelflaed page (the Mercia infobox says 'Annexed by Wessex: 918'); Cliopatria says 925. The one predecessor is anglo-saxon-england (its successors name Mercia with the 534 shape); the infobox's 'Sub-Roman Britain', 'Hwicce' and 'Kingdom of Lindsey' are not predecessors (Mercia absorbed Hwicce and Lindsey later). Mercia starts 527 and anglo-saxon-england ends 533 with a 527 split for Essex but none for Mercia, so the land is claimed twice for 527-533. Rulers are omitted: only the first and last entries of the page's list were read. Not settled / unverified (page budget 9 spent on the Mercia, Trent, Wulfhere, Supremacy, Offa, Egbert, Ceolwulf, Aethelflaed and Danelaw pages): the 617 and 628 growth beyond the Hwicce; the 692 and 840 additions around London and Essex; the 757/763 loss of the Thames border strip; the 866 loss of Lindsey; the 875 drop; Coenwulf's years 796-821 beyond Kent and East Anglia, Beornwulf's accession and Berhtwulf (840-852) are not on the pages read, so the 806-824 shape is judged only against 825. Surrey (a sub-kingdom under Wulfhere, charter 673-675) and the Magonsæte (Merewalh, subking under Wulfhere; 'no record of an independent ruler after 740') have no Cliopatria row. Disagreements: Lindsey lost to Northumbria in 661 (Mercian Supremacy) or 674 (Wulfhere); Nottingham ceded 867 and taken 868 (Danelaw) or occupied 868 (Mercia); end of Mercian control of Kent 796 (Offa) or 825 (Mercia, Egbert). Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Mercia' residue shapes 884-925 sit in the same Wessex shape as the western half. The Danelaw page gives no Thames-Lea-Watling Street line. Region names: only Cliopatria shapes, Isle of Wight, Derby and the places London, Oxford and Leicester are used; all resolve. Repaired 2026-10-25 after review: Kent and East Anglia spans split at the breaks the Offa, Kingdom of Kent and Kingdom of East Anglia pages give (Kent 776-785 and 796-798, East Anglia 796-c. 799); Mercia's own client status under Wessex added as vassal_start 879 and vassal_end December 918 (counterpart = the overlord, the reverse of the 726-752 and 786-802 pairs); the Isle of Wight loss moved from 666 to 661 and the Meon valley added to the 661 gain and loss; the 705 gain split into Powys (5 cells), Gwynedd (5) and Gwent (1); the 800 keyframe subtracts Wessex's 787 shape and the three Thames cells enter Mercia by a 806 gain from Wessex (confidence 1, page silent). Kent's direct rule 807-825 (Coenwulf page) is not split off.
